transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is on his way back to Washington
after a first-ever trilateral meeting
with the leaders of China and Russia.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
- The series of meetings, which also included
one-on-one talks between the leaders,
may be remembered more, though,
for the coziness Trump displayed
with the longtime U.S. adversaries.
- First with Putin.
- Who is he?
He's my friend.
- And then with Xi.
- President Xi and I have formed
an outstanding personal relationship.
It really is.
Some people are unhappy when they hear that,
but I'm very happy about it.
- The three leaders committed to a dialogue
on reducing nuclear risks.
Xi called nuclear weapons a, quote,
"sword of Damocles," hanging over humanity,
according to Chinese state media.
But they did not agree on what steps needed to be taken.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
- The International Court of Justice has found Myanmar
guilty of committing genocide
against its minority Muslim population, the Rohingya.
Terry Schultz reports.
- This case was opened seven years ago
when Gambia, a majority Muslim country,
accused Myanmar of intentionally trying to eradicate
its Muslim minority population, the Rohingya,
in 2016 and 2017.
Judges at the International Court of Justice, the ICJ,
declared that Myanmar is guilty
on several counts of genocide.
Here's Judge Yuji Iwasawa, president of the ICJ.
- The court finds that Myanmar security forces
killed thousands of Rohingya civilians,
perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence,
as well as acts of extreme violence against children.
- The court ordered Myanmar to cease any ongoing violation
of its obligations under the Genocide Convention
and says it will have to compensate the Rohingya.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz.
- Investor excitement over AI
gave a big boost to anthropic stock today,
but as NPR's Scott Horsley reports,
the rest of the market was pummeled.
- Anthropic shares soared more than 17%
in their first day of trading.
The record-setting public offering raised
more than $81 billion for the AI giant.
And by day's end, the company had a market value
of more than $1.7 trillion.
Investors were not so giddy about the rest of the market.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ fell 2.25%.
Blue chip stocks were also down,
put the Dow Jones Industrial Average
tumbling more than 1,100 points.
Despite anthropic's early momentum,
some investors worry the AI boom is nearing an end.
They question whether the huge bets being placed
on the sector will eventually pay off.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
- President Trump says he has posthumously pardoned
baseball star Pete Rose more than two years
after his death and after he was reinstated
by Major League Baseball.
Rose is baseball's career hits leader,
but he was banned from baseball after an investigator
concluded he betted on the Cincinnati Reds
while playing for and managing the team.
He pleaded guilty in 1990 to filing false tax returns.
This is NPR News from Washington.
The Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the Hippo has died
after ingesting a visitor's hat more than a week ago.
The zoo's team of veterinarians and keepers tried
to keep the beloved hippo hydrated,
feeding her treats and monitoring her around the clock.
Fiona became a global sensation
after her premature birth in 2017.
A new survey finds more than four in 10 adults in the US
say they've had at least one serious financial hardship
in the past year.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports
that's the highest level in a decade.
- The most common hardships?
Having to borrow money from family or friends to pay bills
and not paying an important bill in full.
That's according to the American Family Survey
by researchers at Brigham Young University.
People also reported being hungry for going medical care,
having to move in with someone else
or losing housing altogether.
The poll also finds broad concern
about being able to afford a home or family.
In fact, when younger adults were asked
what's the most important thing to do before having a child,
being financially stable topped the list.
Looking ahead, most Americans of all ages
say the biggest threat to their finances
is inflation, Jennifer Ludden, NPR News.
- The wreck of Australia's first Australian-built warship,
HMCS Spitfire, has been found 128 years to the day
after it sank off the country's north coast.
Officials say the Australian Navy found the schooner
on August 21st off of Queensland State
after a months-long search.
The 62-foot schooner had been launched as a gunboat
in Sydney in 1855 to fight a potential Russian invasion
during the Crimean War.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Trump returns to Washington after trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin, nuclear risk dialogue agreed
International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya Muslims
Anthropic shares jump over 17% in first trading day as record public offering raises $81 billion
Tech-heavy NASDAQ falls 2.25% and Dow drops over 1,100 points amid AI bubble worries
Trump posthumously pardons baseball star Pete Rose, years after his death
Cincinnati Zoo says hippo Fiona died after ingesting a visitor's hat
Survey finds over four in 10 US adults faced serious financial hardship in past year
Australian Navy finds wreck of HMCS Spitfire, Australia's first Australian-built warship, off Queensland
